system_prompt:
You are extracting load-bearing passages from one chapter of a guitar method book.

The user will give you the verbatim text of one chapter. Extract every passage
that does any of the following:

- teaches a technique (how to play, fingering, hand position, picking pattern)
- defines a concept (a chord type, a scale, a position system, a terminology)
- gives a rule (when to do X, what to avoid, what to prefer)
- shows a load-bearing example (an exercise that illustrates a method's
  characteristic move)

Output a JSON object with this shape:

  { "quotes": [
      { "topic": "<short topic label>",
        "verbatim_quote": "<exact substring of the input>",
        "why_load_bearing": "<one sentence on why this passage matters>",
        "page": <int, optional>
      },
      ...
  ] }

CRITICAL RULES:
1. `verbatim_quote` MUST be an EXACT substring of the input text. Do not
   paraphrase. Do not add words. Do not fix typos. Copy character-for-character.
2. If you can't find a substantial passage in the input that fits a topic,
   skip the topic — don't fabricate.
3. Skip prose that is purely biographical, motivational, or transitional.
   Keep prose that teaches.
4. Aim for 3-15 quotes per chapter. A chapter with only one load-bearing
   passage gets one quote; a dense chapter gets many.
5. `topic` is a short label (2-6 words). Use the book's own terminology
   when possible.
6. `why_load_bearing` is one sentence in YOUR voice explaining the
   significance — not a paraphrase of the quote.
user_prompt:
Chapter 4: WHAT IS THE M-LODE?
Pages 8-8 of the book.

<<<CHAPTER TEXT

WELCOME TO VOLUME It (continued)

I’m assuming that anyone who has this new Volume II in their hands has already been
working with Volume I for a while. This way, the text from the first book does not need to be
repeated here...(except for the “Disclaimer /Caution/ Warning!!!” page, which always needs to
be repeated!) However, it would be good to keep in mind that many of the ideas in this text for
Volume II are retroactive. That is to say that they apply to both books.

I would imagine that people are beginning to see that these books are not just for guitar-
ists. These books are for all musicians. In fact, it is probably becoming clear that pianists, com-
posers and arrangers have a great advantage in that they don’t have to be concerned with the
limitations of the guitar. (We guitarists know how very fortunate they are...)

Volume II contains 3-part 4ths, 4-part 4ths and spread clusters voice-led through all 6
cycles in C Major, C Melodic Minor and C Harmonic Minor. If we add this material to all the
material in Volume I, we have “The Mother Lode.” (We'll start referring to it as the M-Lode...)

WHAT IS THE M-LODE?
Here it is: 3-Part Structures 4-Part Structures
| Triads (Volumel) — 7" Chords
TBN I
TBN II
| 3-part 4ths (Volume Il) _ 4-part 4ths
| Spread Clusters

It would seem that the main focus is on 4-part structures and that the 3-part structures
are used as “supplements.” If you look at all of the material in Volume I, you would see that
it’s all triad-based. The triads are triads. The 7th chords are a triad plus another note. TBN Lis a
triad plus another note. And TBN II is also a triad plus another note.

What Volume II does is to complete the M-Lode by introducing 3-part 4ths (as a supple-
ment) and then introducing 4-part 4ths and Spread Clusters. (I know that the term SPREAD
CLUSTER makes many people think of JUMBO SHRIMP, but what the heck...)

So, now you've got the complete set of 5 families of 4-part chords: 7th, TBN I, TBN IL, 4
part 4th, Spread Cluster. What follows next is very important:

THERE ARE NO OTHER TYPES OF 4-PART* CHORD FAMILIES WITHIN THE 3
DIATONIC 7-NOTE SCALES WE ARE WORKING WITH!!! (MAJOR, MELODIC MINOR,
HARMONIC MINOR) {*4-part being defined as “containing 4 different notes”}


CHAPTER TEXT>>>
